name: Enterprise Rent-A-Car
verdict: Enterprise Rent-A-Car is part of Enterprise Holdings (branded Enterprise Mobility), the holding company the Taylor family created for its car-rental portfolio. In July 2019 a U.S. Department of Labor administrative law judge found the Baltimore subsidiary unlawfully discriminated against African-American job applicants; in November 2021 the Department's Administrative Review Board unanimously reversed that ruling and remanded the case. On hold for a maintainer.
note: Rating note: on hold for a maintainer. The link is sourced (Taylor family holding company; second source: the parties' stipulation in the DOL case, 'Enterprise is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Enterprise Holdings, Inc.'). The company record is contested: on 17 July 2019 a DOL administrative law judge ordered Enterprise RAC Company of Baltimore LLC to pay $6.6M to 2,336 rejected African-American applicants after finding a pattern and practice of hiring discrimination in its management-trainee programme between 2007 and 2017, plus debarment from federal contracts (WBAL-TV, 1 Aug 2019, opened via the Wayback Machine; also Automotive Fleet, 6 Aug 2019). On 3 November 2021 the Department's Administrative Review Board unanimously reversed the entirety of that ruling — finding the ALJ applied the wrong legal standards — and remanded the case to a different ALJ (EASI, 24 Jun 2022; DirectEmployers, 31 May 2022); the outcome on remand is not sourced here. If the 2019 ALJ finding counts as the company's record, the tier is concern (a company finding); if the 2021 reversal means no standing finding, the tier is none. Draft why in PR #1104.
